samples.question: When did the Directive on Automated Decision-Making take effect, and by when was compliance required?
samples.ground_truth: The Directive took effect on April 1, 2019, with compliance required by April 1, 2020.
contexts: [P01 Directive purpose, effective date and scope] The objective of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making is to ensure that Automated Decision Systems are deployed in a manner that reduces risks to Canadians and federal institutions, and leads to more efficient, accurate, consistent, and interpretable decisions made pursuant to Canadian law. The Directive took effect on April 1, 2019, with compliance required by no later than April 1, 2020. It applies to any system, tool, or statistical model used to recommend or make an administrative decision about a client. It applies only to systems in production and excludes Automated Decision Systems operating in test environments. It does not apply to any National Security Systems. It applies to any Automated Decision System developed or procured after April 1, 2020.

[P06 Quality assurance: bias testing and outcome monitoring] Before launching into production, departments must develop processes so that the data and information used by the Automated Decision Systems are tested for unintended data biases and other factors that may unfairly impact the outcomes. Departments must develop processes to monitor the outcomes of Automated Decision Systems to safeguard against unintentional outcomes and to verify compliance with institutional and program legislation, as well as this Directive, on a scheduled basis.

[P02 Algorithmic Impact Assessment duties] The Assistant Deputy Minister responsible for the program using the Automated Decision System is responsible for completing an Algorithmic Impact Assessment prior to the production of any Automated Decision System. They must apply the relevant requirements prescribed in Appendix C as determined by the Algorithmic Impact Assessment. They must update the Algorithmic Impact Assessment when system functionality or the scope of the Automated Decision System changes. They must release the final results of Algorithmic Impact Assessments in an accessible format via Government of Canada websites and any other services designated by the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat pursuant to the Directive on Open Government.

[P08 Human intervention and approvals] Departments must ensure that an Automated Decision System allows for human intervention, when appropriate, as per Appendix C. They must obtain the appropriate level of approvals prior to the production of an Automated Decision System as per Appendix C.

[P05 Source code release and documenting decisions] Departments must release custom source code owned by the Government of Canada as per the Directive on Service and Digital, unless the source code is processing data classified SECRET, TOP SECRET or PROTECTED C, disclosure would otherwise be exempted or excluded under the Access to Information Act, or an exemption is provided by the Chief Information Officer of Canada. Departments must document the decisions of Automated Decision Systems in accordance with the Directive on Service and Digital, and in support of the monitoring and reporting requirements.

[P07 Data quality, peer review, training, security, legal] Departments must validate that the data collected for, and used by, the Automated Decision System is relevant, accurate, up to date, and in accordance with the Policy on Service and Digital and the Privacy Act. They must consult the appropriate qualified expert to review the Automated Decision System as prescribed in Appendix C. They must provide adequate employee training in the design, function, and implementation of the Automated Decision System to be able to review, explain and oversee its operations. They must establish contingency systems and processes, conduct risk assessments during the development cycle and establish appropriate safeguards as per the Policy on Government Security, and consult with the institution's legal services from the concept stage of a project to ensure compliant use of the Automated Decision System.
samples.answer: The Directive on Automated Decision-Making took effect on April 1, 2019. Compliance with the directive was required by no later than April 1, 2020.
